title: Fine-grained Canary Scheduler & Policy DSL
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a fine-grained canary rollout scheduler and policy engine that supports traffic splits, step schedules, shadow traffic, A/B cohorts, and automatic rollback guardrails. The goal is a predictable, auditable, and reversible rollout primitive that integrates with the Console, API, and the serving runtime. The engine must: (1) accept a declarative rollout DSL (YAML/JSON) for traffic steps and guardrails, (2) provide runtime enforcement to route traffic and pause/rollback automatically based on metrics, and (3) surface clear signals and manual override controls in the Console. This ticket covers the core scheduling and decision logic, the policy evaluation loop, and integration points; UI/UX polish and extended canary experiment analytics will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: A declarative rollout schema is defined and documented (example configs included)
Runtime module can apply traffic splits to live model variants deterministically (hashing-based bucketing)
Policy engine evaluates guardrails (latency P95, error-rate, model-quality evals) every step and marks step PASS/FAIL/PAUSE
Automatic rollback triggers run reliably with hysteresis to avoid flapping
Shadow traffic support: ability to mirror X% of traffic to candidate variant without impacting responses
Console shows rollout state (current split, history, last evaluation) and allows immediate pause/rollback
Integration tests covering scheduled ramps, guardrail breaches, manual override, and shadow mirroring
progress_updates: 2026-02-10: Created ticket and initial schema draft for rollout DSL (see docs link)
2026-02-18: Prototype deterministic bucketing implemented in runtime routing layer; unit tests for bucket consistency added
2026-02-25: First pass of guardrail evaluator implemented: supports error-rate and latency metrics from Prometheus; hooked into policy loop
2026-03-03: Implemented pause-on-breach and simple auto-rollback with 3-step hysteresis to prevent oscillation
2026-03-09: End-to-end flow tested in staging with shadow traffic; identified an edge case where short-lived backend spikes caused false-positive rollbacks
2026-03-12: Mitigation added — configurable evaluation window and minimum request count before verdict; preparing integration test matrix
decisions: Use deterministic hashing on user_id (fall back to request id) for stable bucketing across replicas
Metric sources: initially support Prometheus and Datadog; abstract a metrics adapter for future backends
Guardrail semantics: PASS/FAIL/PAUSE with configurable thresholds and evaluation window; default window = 3 minutes
Rollback policy: require failure for N consecutive evaluations or X absolute delta vs baseline depending on metric type
Expose both a declarative DSL and a simple API; Console will translate user inputs into DSL for storage in control plane
notes: Edge-case: when a single user generates high volume requests, bucketing noise can bias short windows — consider weighted sampling or per-user rate caps
We need a canary audit log that records bucket assignments and policy decisions to satisfy compliance requests for Private customers
Plan for future: add quality guardrails that run model outputs against a reference prompt set and compute semantic drift (requires evaluation infra)
